questions.question: Is silver considered a toxic metal?
questions.answer: Silver (Ag) is listed among the minor toxic metals for which toxicity has been described, according to [[sources/ufelle2021-metals-chapter|Ufelle & Barchowsky 2021]]. Beyond noting it as a metal with described toxicity, this page does not yet detail specific silver health effects.

questions.question: Does this page explain how much silver is in food or what health effects it causes?
questions.answer: Not yet. The toxicology chapter this page draws on does not provide a detailed silver subsection, so the page currently serves only as source-map context. Substantive silver-specific information awaits a dedicated ingest of the literature.

questions.question: Why is the silver page so short?
questions.answer: This page is a source-map stub created during the re-ingest of [[sources/ufelle2021-metals-chapter|Ufelle & Barchowsky 2021]], which mentions silver only as a minor toxic metal without a dedicated section. As stated on the page, substantive silver-specific expansion awaits a dedicated ingest of source literature.

questions.question: What source is this silver page based on?
questions.answer: The page currently draws on a single source, [[sources/ufelle2021-metals-chapter|Ufelle & Barchowsky 2021]], the "Toxic Effects of Metals" chapter (Ch 23) in Casarett & Doull's Essentials of Toxicology, 4th ed. That chapter references silver among minor toxic metals but does not provide a detailed silver-specific subsection.
